flagged.evidence: The step says, “The matrix ρ(d) has rational entries and finite order |D|.” For a nontrivial cyclic D and the trivial Q-representation, ρ(d)=I has order 1, not |D|. Only ρ(d)^|D|=I follows. The ensuing root-of-unity conclusion remains repairable, but the stated order claim is false.

Step 4.1 says Frobenius reciprocity gives ⟨Res_C^G x,U_E^C⟩_C=⟨Res_E^G x,1_E⟩_E. The cited dependency states instead “⟨Ind_H^G χ,ψ⟩_G=⟨χ,Res_H^G ψ⟩_H.” The displayed equality needs Hermitian symmetry (or F1, using rational-valuedness) on both sides; F2 alone has the opposite argument order.

The proof says that U_j(g_i)≠0, together with the ordering and minimality of i, “forces j=i.” This does not follow for j<i: minimality only gives a_j=0. For G=C4, order the representatives C4 before its subgroup C2; for a generator g_i of C2, U_{C4}(g_i)=1 although j≠i. The evaluation proof works after restricting to terms with a_j≠0, so this is a small repair.
